title: Scene Review
description: The hand-written half of a Sign-Off report (design/scene-signoff.md). One per scene, in reviews/<scene>.json, rendered into reviews/<scene>.html by tools/scene-signoff/report.mjs. NOT the record of record: a scene's authoritative review state is `authoring.review` on the episode's own scene entry, written only by tools/scene-signoff/seal.mjs. This file is the reasoning and the prose; that one is the verdict. Where they disagree the episode file is right.

id.description: The scene brief's id, matching the filename.

sceneRef.description: The scene's own id inside its episode's scenes[] array.

asks.description: What the review needs from Ingram, as plain questions. Rendered in the loudest block on the page, above the analysis, because they are the only part that blocks her. Never a check id: a review that says "P3 is unresolved" has done the work and delivered none of it (her own correction, 2026-09-22). Every ask must carry `current`, at least two `options` with their implications, and a `recommendation` -- required by the schema so that an under-specified question cannot be shipped.

question.description: One question, naming the specific thing being asked. It should be answerable without reading the detail below it.

detail.description: The evidence and the options, in the small markdown subset tools/scene-signoff/report.mjs renders.

blocking.description: True when the seal cannot happen until this is answered. Shown on the card, and counted in the header.

current.description: What is true right now, stated before any option -- the state of the data, the lore, the map, whatever the question is actually about. Ingram, 2026-09-22: "you need to give me full context for decisions you want me to make, it's still a bit confusing what question 1 is asking me to decide/confirm." A question with no `current` is the failure that correction names: it tells her something is missing without telling her enough to decide.

options.description: The real alternatives, each with what choosing it commits to. Two minimum: a question with one option is a request for permission, not a decision, and should be phrased as one.

label.description: The choice, in a few words.

implication.description: What it commits to, what it costs, and what it forecloses.

recommendation.description: Which option I would take and why. Stating it is not pre-empting the decision -- it is the difference between handing over a question and handing over homework.

passes.description: One entry per pass. `proposed` is my verdict; it renders as "proposed" and never as recorded, because CLEAR is assent and only Ingram gives it.

applied.description: Changes already made to the scene, with their diffs. Nothing here needs approval -- it was obvious, non-semantic, or Ingram asked for it.

proposed.description: My verdict for this pass. A recorded verdict on the episode file always outranks it.

recorded.description: Informational only -- the render reads the episode file for this, never this field.

summary.description: One sentence, rendered large above the body. The thing to read if nothing else gets read.

body.description: The pass's analysis, in the rendered markdown subset.

declined.description: Recommended checks deliberately declined, each with its reason. Declining every one of them is still a legitimate CLEAR -- they are offers, not debt.

what.description: What is absent, in plain words.

why.description: Why that is right for this scene.

findings.description: Quality pass only. At most five, ranked by how much each would change what happens at the table.

severity.description: applied: fixed, diff shown. noted: a real observation deliberately left alone, on the record so it is not mistaken for an oversight. ok: checked and found sound. open: proposed and waiting on Ingram.

judgedFine.description: What was considered and found sound, named so that silence is not mistaken for inattention.

before.description: The text as it was. Rendered as the minus side of a diff.

after.description: The text as it now is, or as proposed. Rendered as the plus side.
